verdicts.title: Introduction to tropical algebraic geometry
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: This is an expository introduction to tropical algebraic geometry based on my lectures at the Workshop on Tropical Geometry and Integrable Systems in Glasgow, July 4-8, 2011, and at the ELGA 2011 school on Algebraic Geometry and Applications in Buenos Aires, August 1-5, 2011.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes an 'expository introduction to tropical algebraic geometry' from lecture notes, which shares vocabulary with the conjecture but makes no claims about tropicalized cohomology rank or resolution proof width.

verdicts.title: Counting Algebraic Curves with Tropical Geometry
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
Tropical geometry is a piecewise linear "shadow" of algebraic geometry. It allows for the computation of several cohomological invariants of an algebraic variety. In particular, its application to enumerative algebraic geometry led to significant progress.

verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes tropical geometry techniques for algebraic curve counting (Severi varieties, Hurwitz numbers, enumerative geometry) and makes no mention of d-regular graphs, resolution proof width, or any link to Boolean satisfiability / proof complexity.

verdicts.title: Amoebas of algebraic varieties and tropical geometry
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: This survey consists of two parts. Part 1 is devoted to amoebas. These are images of algebraic subvarieties in the complex torus under the logarithmic moment map. The amoebas have essentially piecewise-linear shape if viewed at large. Furthermore, they degenerate to certain piecewise-linear objects
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a survey on amoebas and their piecewise-linear degenerations in tropical geometry, with no mention of cohomology rank, graphs, or resolution proof width.
